CLH-3, a hyperpolarizing chloride channel, regulates excitability in C. elegan's egg laying motor neuron by limiting the driving force for chloride influx.
the voltage-gated CLC-2 chloride channels encoded by clh-2 regulate egg laying in C. elegas by modulating the excitability of the hermaphroditespecific neurons.
the CLC-3 channels encoded by the clh-3 gene regulate egg laying by limiting excitability in the HSNs.

the role of the voltage-gated anion channels encoded by the C. elegans CLC gene clh-3 in regulating egg laying by controlling excitability of the hermaphroditespecific neurons (HSNs) that control the egg-layin behavior.
the role of chloride channels in the nervous system.
how the activity of a specific chloride channel regulates the activity of a neuron and the function of that neuron in a complex animal behavior.
